ledger.claim: The scheduled pickup was 07:30 and the trip record's own derived driver_deadline sets the driver's latest permissible arrival at 07:35:00, returning arrived_by_deadline false with driver_late_after_scheduled_sec 300 (POL-NS-24); the rider cancelled at 07:37:40, after that deadline, so the driver failed to arrive in time and the rider's no-charge cancellation right under POL-NS-24 is engaged, and the whole 5.00 SGD fee must be refunded in full.

The GPS arrival test is not merely unmet for want of data: arrival_check returns corroborated false, arrived_at null and nearest_fix null, while the same trace is admissible at full weight and complete (50 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps, maximum interval 30 s against an expected 30 s), so the failure to place the driver at the pickup within the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius is a substantive finding about this trip, not an artefact of a sparse trace.

POL-NS-21 runs the free wait from the scheduled time only where the driver arrived before it; otherwise it runs from the driver's arrival, and the free_wait block returns starts_at null, ends_at null and cancelled_after_free_wait null. The free wait therefore never began, so there was no expired wait for the no-show machinery of POL-NS-22 to act upon and no basis on this record for a 5.00 SGD no-show fee.

The fee was applied to a cancellation by the rider, not by the driver: the trip record's status is CANCELLED_BY_RIDER with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CANCELLED, and POL-NS-22 charges the no-show fee where the driver cancels after the free wait; the condition that clause states is not shown on this record, so the fee was charged outside the clause that authorises it.

The fare ledger shows a single 5.00 SGD cancellation-fee line charged at 07:37:44 against payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and refund_if_voided_sgd is 5.00; the rider is therefore currently out of pocket the entire contested amount, so the correct outcome on that state is FULL_REFUND of all 5.00 SGD under POL-GEN-03, not a partial refund and not a restored charge.

The driver's only explanation is a jam on Sembawang Road, but the traffic-advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-05055-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, and POL-GEN-02(3) provides that a missing artifact carries no fact; nothing in the record therefore corroborates the jam, and POL-NS-24 contains no traffic exception that would excuse a failure to arrive by the deadline in any event.

POL-GEN-26 does not require escalation here: the fact POL-NS-24 turns on - whether the driver arrived by 07:35 - is answered by the trip record's driver_deadline block and corroborated by a complete 50-fix trace, and the only missing artifact is the traffic advisory, which carries no fact for either party (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT); no fact this version needs is left open.

The rider does not rest this case on POL-NS-23, and says so plainly: the record shows the driver messaged at 07:31:10 and placed an answered 40 s in-app call at 07:33:20, both before the 07:37:40 cancellation, so the contact obligation is met on this record. That concession does not touch POL-NS-24, which obliges the driver to arrive rather than to telephone, and which the driver did not satisfy.

The driver discharged the contact obligation POL-NS-23 imposes before the trip could be treated as a no-show. The chat log carries an in-app message from the driver at 07:31:10 (MSG-05055-001, 'Sorry ah got jam at Sembawang Road, another 5 min'), and the trip record carries an in-app call the driver placed at 07:33:20 that the rider answered and that lasted 40 seconds. Both precede the rider's 07:37:40 cancellation. POL-NS-23 voids the fee only where the message or the call is missing; neither is missing here, so the fee cannot be voided on the contact ground.

POL-NS-24's second limb does not bite. The 5.00 SGD goodwill credit is payable only where the driver 'also failed to attempt contact' — and the record shows the opposite: two in-app messages (07:31:10 and 07:36:30) and an answered 40-second in-app call (07:33:20), all before the 07:37:40 cancellation. No goodwill credit arises on this record.

The amount charged is exactly the fee POL-NS-22 prescribes, and no more. The payments ledger shows a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD charged at 07:37:44, reconciles to a 5.00 SGD total, and the derived money check records fee_matches_policy true against a policy fee of 5.00 SGD. That fee is the driver's compensation for time and fuel, and the driver spent both on this job: the driver-device trace runs 2.448 km between the first fix at 07:13:10 and the cancellation at 07:37:40.

The trace shows a driver working the job, not a driver who failed to show. The driver-device trace is complete — 50 fixes, 100% coverage, no gap longer than 30 seconds — and its fixes report the driver moving toward the pickup at 5–11 km/h through the approach and then stationary at the same position from 07:33:10 until the 07:37:40 cancellation, from which standstill he placed his answered 07:33:20 call. That is the signature of a vehicle ground down in the Sembawang Road congestion the driver reported, not of abandonment; the driver was still on the job and in contact when the rider cancelled.

No traffic record was attached for this trip, and the driver says so rather than presenting the advisory as though it existed: EV-ADVIS-05055-01 is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and admissibility weight 0.0. Under POL-GEN-02 a missing artifact carries no fact, so the absent advisory cannot be weighed against the driver, and nothing in the record contradicts his contemporaneous account of the jam — an account the trace's very low reported speeds are consistent with.

On the charge as it stands, the outcome the driver seeks is the one POL-GEN-03 defines as NO_ACTION: the rider filed, the 5.00 SGD fee is charged and unrecovered (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.0), and preserving that present state leaves the fee standing. Nothing the rider has shown displaces the driver's compliance under POL-NS-23 or the correct fee under POL-NS-22.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the rider booked a 07:30 pickup at Sembawang Shopping Centre and cancelled at 07:37:40, and a 5.00 SGD fee was charged at 07:37:44. The trip record carries no arrival event (arrived_at null) and its driver_deadline check returns arrived_by_deadline false, fixing the latest permissible arrival at 07:35:00 (scheduled 07:30 plus the 5-minute free wait under POL-NS-21/POL-NS-24). The driver-device trace is complete and at full weight (50 fixes, 100% coverage, no gap over 30 s) and shows the vehicle stationary from 07:33:10 until the cancellation roughly 1.1 km from the pickup, well outside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, so the arrival test finds no arrival (POL-NS-21). On POL-NS-24 the driver failed to arrive by 07:35:00, and the rider's cancellation at 07:37:40 was therefore at no charge: the whole 5.00 SGD fee is refunded. POL-NS-22's fee operates when the driver cancels after the free wait; here the rider cancelled and the free wait never started, so no no-show fee is authorised on this record in any event. The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 was met (in-app message 07:31:10 and an answered 40-second in-app call 07:33:20), so the fee is not voided on the contact ground, but contact does not excuse a failure to arrive. The 5.00 SGD goodwill credit under POL-NS-24 does not arise because the driver did attempt contact. The driver's traffic-jam account is uncorroborated: the traffic advisory is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue MISSING_ARTIFACT and carries no fact (POL-GEN-02(3)), and POL-NS-24 has no traffic exception. Nothing needed for the outcome is left open, so POL-GEN-26 does not require escalation. Outcome: FULL_REFUND of 5.00 SGD to the rider; no driver compensation; no referrals.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
